native_mechanisms: A single rolling sphere (one accumulator) is the sole carried memory across the whole ordered input, with no table, history, or backward reference to prior positions.

Each mark is pressed into the sphere and then mixed by a fixed count of tumbles/strikes down the trail — rotation-and-crack mixing (add/rotate/xor, no multiply) applied a fixed number of times before the next mark is taken.
Only the final hairline crack in the last stalk is kept as the output token; all intermediate cracks, dust and footprints are discarded on purpose.
One disagreeing mark reshapes the whole sphere, not a sliver — every downstream stalk cracks differently (full-state avalanche from any single input difference).
core_technique: Multi-lane ARX streaming hash: per-8-byte-lane xor + add-rotl(29) + xor-rotl(47) over 32-byte (or AVX2 64-byte) blocks with an overlapping tail block, folded into four seeded words and finalised by SpookyHash's 12-step ShortEnd rotate/xor/add chain, returning one state word.
